system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:40 UTC, WS-DWELLS-01 used the explicit proxy for a successful HTTPS CONNECT to download.windowsupdate.com. The recorded user agent is Windows Update Agent, and the tunnel transferred about 41.8 MB from the server to the client.
The Windows Update traffic is consistent with patch-related activity, but these records do not identify who initiated it or establish that the organization's approved patch procedure was followed.

At 13:40 and 14:10 UTC, WS-DWELLS-01 made SMB connections to DC-LV-01, with successful network logons recorded as the workstation machine account. The evidence does not identify a share or file accessed.

At 14:15 UTC, domain records show dana.wells requesting a ticket for WS-KORTEGA-01$ from 10.20.20.30, and WS-KORTEGA-01 records a network logon for dana.wells from that same address. Network telemetry identifies 10.20.20.30 as the proxy endpoint, making the source attribution noteworthy but not explaining it.

At 14:19 UTC, process-termination events on WS-DWELLS-01 identify Google Drive File Stream and Palo Alto GlobalProtect processes under dana.wells. These are notable against the supplied approval context, but the records do not establish when they started or why they were present.
The supplied records do not document a PowerShell process or command around the reported time; the collection gap prevents treating that absence as evidence that PowerShell did not run.

known_telemetry_limitations: Windows Event Forwarding was stopped for WS-DWELLS-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so its Security and Sysmon events for the time encompassing the reported PowerShell appearance were not collected.
The available network records show connections and limited proxy metadata, not the PowerShell command, script contents, or the files accessed over SMB.
The supplied evidence does not explain why dana.wells authenticated to WS-KORTEGA-01 from 10.20.20.30, an address also identified as the proxy endpoint.
claims_not_established: Whether the reported PowerShell window was benign IT activity, malicious execution, or another process being mistaken for PowerShell.
What command or script, if any, ran on WS-DWELLS-01, and what account or process launched it.
Whether the Windows Update download was part of authorized workstation patching or was initiated by another actor or process.
Whether dana.wells's 14:15 network logon to WS-KORTEGA-01 was authorized, and why its recorded source address is the proxy endpoint.
Whether Google Drive File Stream or GlobalProtect had an approved exception or were involved in the reported activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover local Security and Sysmon event logs from WS-DWELLS-01 for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including process creation and termination events.
Collect PowerShell Operational logs, including script block and module logging if available, and endpoint detection or process telemetry for WS-DWELLS-01.
Verify Windows Update history, patch deployment records, and the activity of WS-KORTEGA-01 during the review window against the change calendar.
Review FILE-LV-01 and DC-LV-01 SMB auditing or file-access logs to identify the share and files involved in the SMB connections.
Investigate the 14:15 authentication using WS-KORTEGA-01 session and process logs, DC authentication records, and network/IP assignment or proxy configuration data.
Check software inventory and authorization records for Google Drive File Stream and GlobalProtect on WS-DWELLS-01.
